proposals.evidence: The Noiri/Dungra elḍ- turmeric noun compares with Gujarati haḷad and Hindi haladdī in Turner’s haridrā branch. This placement allows initial h loss, contraction and the recorded initial e vowel; it is a regional lexical comparison, with the o/a endings retained and no claim to a newly established sound law.

proposals.evidence: Turner gives Gujarati kā̃dɔ, Marathi kā̃dā and Konkani kā̃ndo onion under kanda bulbous root. These western survey kāṇḍ-/kand- and devoiced kānt- forms fit that bulb/onion family; source nasal/retroflex spellings are preserved. They are separated from the granthi knot-derived gaṇḍ-/gaṇṭh- onion words.
